page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this server features 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2678.09 placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory performance generally fall within the average range. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 10778.72 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5922.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, measuring 57.86 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 40.87 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Performance bottlenecks are evident in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and prompt processing for medium-sized (7B) language models, both of which scored in the bottom 25%.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of excess compute cores. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is suited for workloads such as database operations, caching layers, web serving, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks. It is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded decompression or medium-to-large scale LLM inference.
